angularDiameterSource: Computed here from the record's radius and distance: 2 x 222,624 km at 148.91 pc = 0.02 mas. No interferometric diameter of this star is used.
distanceSource: Gaia DR3 parallax 6.7154 +/- 0.0401 mas (same row, RUWE 1.00): 148.91 pc, no zero-point correction
radiusSource: Radius 0.32 +/- 0.07 solar radii from Adams et al. 2021, the stellar radius of the default parameter set of EPIC 228836835 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2021PSJ.....2..152A/abstract): 222,624 km at 695,700 km per solar radius. Mass 0.418179 +/- 0.020881 solar masses from TICv8, the stellar mass of EPIC 228836835 b's parameter set from TICv8 (the default leaves it empty) in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2019AJ....158..138S/abstract); GM is that mass times the JPL solar GM. Temperature 3782 +/- 152 K from Adams et al. 2021, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of EPIC 228836835 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2021PSJ.....2..152A/abstract). presentationUp: the display axis is a sky-plane convention; the spin axis's position angle on the sky is not measured.
effectiveTemperatureSource: Adams et al. 2021, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of EPIC 228836835 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2021PSJ.....2..152A/abstract)
surfaceGravitySource: log g from the mass and radius in packages/astronomy/data/bodies/epic-228836835.json (sources in its physicalNotes), log10(GM/R^2) in cgs: 5.049, rounded to two decimals
